scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

So, I created a new profile for him on my Switch so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept him distracted and allowed me to focus on my studies without worrying about him accidentally deleting my games or progress. But then, when I got back to school, I started getting annoyed every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop because I had to click on my profile each time. It was a minor inconvenience, but it started to bother me. So, I decided to delete his profile to simplify things and make it easier for me to use my Switch without having to switch profiles every time. Now, fast forward to Thanksgiving. I brought my Switch again for the train ride to my dad's house. My stepbrother picked it up to play, and when he realized his Zelda save was gone, he started freaking out and even cried a little. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete his profile because he was enjoying playing on it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, but now I'm feeling guilty. So, is it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects of this situation. First, ownership. The Nintendo Switch is mine, right? I bought it, and I'm the one who uses it primarily. So, in that sense, I have the right to decide who uses it and under what conditions. Creating a profile for him was a courtesy, not an obligation. On the other hand, by creating a profile for him, I gave him access to the Switch, and he started using it. Deleting his profile without discussing it with him or giving him a chance to save his progress could be seen as unfair or mean. I also need to consider the emotional impact. My stepbrother was really upset when he found out his save was gone. He was enjoying playing on the Switch, and having his progress deleted must have felt like a loss. My dad's reaction also indicates that he thinks it was mean, which adds to the guilt I'm feeling. Another aspect is communication. I didn't talk to my stepbrother about my decision to delete his profile. If I had discussed it with him beforehand, maybe we could have found a solution that worked for both of us, like setting up a shared profile or finding another way for him to play without interfering with my usage. I also need to think about the bigger picture. Relationships, especially with family members, are important. Actions that seem small to me can have a significant impact on others. Building trust and maintaining good relationships require consideration and respect for each other's feelings. In this case, deleting the profile without communication was a unilateral decision that affected my stepbrother negatively. It might have been better to find a compromise or at least inform him about my decision so he could save his progress or find another way to play. So, reflecting on all these points, it seems like deleting the profile without discussing it was not the best decision. It caused unnecessary hurt and tension within the family. It would have been better to communicate my concerns and find a solution that respected both my needs and my stepbrother's enjoyment of the Switch. In the future, I should remember to talk things through and consider how my actions might affect others, especially family members. Good communication can prevent misunderstandings and help maintain harmonious relationships.
